body: I encountered this also but I got it _even using the window close button_ of the non-embedded window. I would also note that this makes it impossible for Godot to write the same OGV file twice: if you set the OGV file as the movie writer filename, run it once (it writes the file), then run it again, the game will freeze on startup trying to write over the same file. I did a bit of digging: the freezing seems to be caused by a combination of two things: 1. Godot's movie writer not properly terminating the OGV file. (As hinted at in [the documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_moviewriter.html#class-moviewriter-private-method-write-end)). This results in an OGV file that has all the frames and can be played by VLC / ingested by FFMPEG, but is technically invalid. 2. Windows explorer trying to index the corrupted file. The process "dllhost.exe" is what has the file open, which is the process used by Explorer to index thumbnails. This is what causes the OS-wide freeze on the file. I discovered #2 by using the "resmon" tool. (I never knew this tool existed but I followed a guide which I will repeat here). 1. Run > "resmon" 2. Go to the CPU tab. 3. Under "Associated Handles" type in the filename (full path not needed). This shows which processes have a lock on that file: The weird thing is that if you try to delete the file in explorer, you don't get an error: simply nothing happens. You can keep using explorer. If you use rm/del on the command line, the command freezes. Eventually, after about 5 minutes, every single attempt to delete the file then succeeds all at once (I get a whole bunch of popups from Explorer saying do you want to delete the file). So the freezing behaviour is not Godot's fault, but it does show that Windows goes insane if you write an unterminated OGV file, so it would be good for Godot's MovieWriter to not do that. Edit: Another key point (a possible workaround) is that this freeze _only happens_ if Windows Explorer looks at the file. If you write the file into a directory that you have no Windows Explorer tab open in (including the Desktop which is always open), the freeze does not occur. Similarly, you can probably delete the file using the command line or any other tool, as long as you do not first open the folder in Explorer.
